derivation: Generated by tools/import_kicad_board.py from the vendor's own KiCad footprint. Pad centres are exact to three decimal places in millimetres, scaled at 8.0 px/mm from a 24.54 x 20.75 mm extent including a 1.0 mm margin. Pin names joined from the symbol library on pad number. Nothing here was measured off an image.
assumption: Every `pin` is null: that field is the rcontrol pin index of a PICSimLab board implementation (webui/pinmap.py), and none exists for this board. `chip_pin` and `chip_index` are what tools/import_pindefs.py read out of the sources named in `pindefs`: the vendor's own CAD, `seeed-pcb`, for `NFC2`, `NFC1`, and the board-support packages for the rest; a pad whose `chip_pin` is null says why in `why_null`. No board module describes nRF54LM20A here, so no level is read for any pad and the pin view reports every one as not modelled until a module and a core exist; `chip_pin` is recorded so that the join is ready, not made. 30 pins on this board are named with NO flat number -- P0.05, P0.04, P0.03, and so on -- so every pad reaching one carries `chip_index` null for that reason and not for a missing reading: no flat GPIO numbering is published for the nRF54LM20A at all, so a module for it would key its own table the way webui/boards/samd21.py does, and until one exists no level is read for any pad here.

pindefs.derivation: Generated by tools/import_pindefs.py from the sources in `packages`, at those revisions, and not every one of them is a board-support package. The vendor's own CAD among them, `seeed-pcb`, answered `NFC2`, `NFC1`; the board-support package, `zephyr`, answered every other pad that resolves. Nothing was inferred from the silkscreen or a pinout image: a label resolves only when every source in `packages` that defines it names the same pin, and `python tools/import_pindefs.py <board>` prints the file that named it. The reason given for each of `SAMD11_RST2`, `SAMD11_SWDIO`, `nRF54_RST`, `nRF54_SWDIO`, `SAMD11_SWCLK`, `nRF54_SWCLK`, `SHPHLD` having no `chip_pin` cites the vendor's own board CAD.

pads.label: SAMD11_RST2
pads.why_null: this pad is named for the on-board debugger, an ATSAMD11D14A, and not for this board's own MCU; `chip_pin` names a pin of the board's MCU, so a number here would be a pin of the wrong chip. NOT claimed: which pin it reaches. No net in Seeed's own board file carries this pad's name, so unlike the SWDIO and SWCLK pads on the same header nothing here was traced

pads.label: SAMD11_SWDIO
pads.why_null: this pad reaches the on-board debugger, an ATSAMD11D14A, and not this board's own MCU; `chip_pin` names a pin of the board's MCU, so a number here would be a pin of the wrong chip. Seeed's own board file names both parts, and the debugger's pins are reachable from it if they are ever wanted under a field that says which chip it means

pads.label: nRF54_RST
pads.why_null: a reset pad of the nRF54LM20A, not a GPIO: Seeed's own nRF54LM20A.kicad_pcb names that part's reset 'nRESET_F2' on the net '~{nRF54_RESET}', apart from all sixty-six of its pads numbered P0.00 through P3.12 by port and bit. A reset is a dedicated pin of the silicon, so there is no GPIO number for this label to have
